newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada sets specials twice at 3.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada sets specials twice at 3.5 percent.

text.p: The Bank of Canada on Monday set two rounds of special purchase and resale agreements in the money market at 3.5 percent, traders said.
The central bank intervened on the money market after the call loan or overnight lending rate traded at the top of the bank's recently raised 3.0-3.5 percent target range for the rate.
"It's artificial upwards pressure with month-end requirements, quarter-end requirements, holiday requirements, all of the above," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage.
Analysts said the move was meant to relieve unwanted pressure on the call loan target band and had no policy implications.
The Government of Canada's three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.21 percent after the intervention.
